title: Transactions and isolation
brief: Choose transactions and isolation from the invariant the writers must preserve.
outcomes: Distinguish atomicity, snapshots and serial outcomes
Choose a sound protocol for one-row and multi-row limits

neighbours.RL91: Owns complete lock protocols, including isolation/snapshot preconditions and waits.

heading.title: A business change
heading.brief: Keep stock, order and lines together; choose boundaries around later payment without implying the card provider joins the database transaction.

heading.title: Snapshots and overlapping writes
heading.brief: Compare statement and transaction snapshots, stale saved updates and write conflicts; label PostgreSQL 18 schedules rather than universalising them.

nested_article.title: Row versions, storage and cleanup
nested_article.brief: Connect logical updates to physical versions and the work required to reclaim them.
outcomes: Explain old-snapshot visibility without in-place overwrite assumptions
Distinguish reusable space, file shrinkage and write amplification

heading.title: A rule across rows
heading.brief: Use the proposed class with two instructors for write skew and bookings for capacity; show why individually valid rows can break a shared rule.

nested_article.title: Locks, contention and deadlocks
nested_article.brief: Design lock scope and ordering so waiting protects the intended decision.
outcomes: Choose a lockable authority with a sound isolation and snapshot protocol
Diagnose and bound contention and deadlocks
nested_article.entry: Transaction snapshots and the class capacity rule.

heading.title: Serializable work
heading.brief: Derive serial outcomes, aborts and complete-transaction retries; compare conditional updates, a shared guard and Serializable for a stated invariant. State which writers participate and which snapshot each decision uses; RL91 develops the guard protocol and its stale-snapshot counterexample.
